entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv17410"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 13</title> <div sID="gen34814" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="2Cor.13.1-2Cor.13.14">2Co 13:1-14</reference>. He Threatens a Severe Proof of His Apostolic Authority, but Prefers They Would Spare Him the Necessity for It.<div eID="gen34814" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34815" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv17410"/><hi type="bold">1. This is the third time I am coming to you--</hi>not merely preparing to come to you. This proves an intermediate visit between the two recorded in <reference osisRef="Acts.18.1">Ac 18:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.20.2">20:2</reference>.<div eID="gen34815" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34816" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established--</hi>Quoted from <reference osisRef="Deut.19.15">De 19:15</reference>, Septuagint. "I will judge not without examination, nor will I abstain from punishing upon due evidence" [Conybeare and Howson]. I will no longer be among you "in all patience" towards offenders (<reference osisRef="2Cor.12.12">2Co 12:12</reference>). The apostle in this case, where ordinary testimony was to be had, does not look for an immediate revelation, nor does he order the culprits to be cast out of the church before his arrival. Others understand the "two or three witnesses" to mean his two or three visits as establishing either (1) the truth of the facts alleged against the offenders, or (2) the reality of his threats. I prefer the first explanation to either of the two latter. <div eID="gen34816" type="x-p"/>

Rather, "I have already said (at my second visit), and tell you (now) beforehand, AS (I did) WHEN I WAS PRESENT THE SECOND TIME, SO also NOW in my absence (the oldest manuscripts omit the 'I write,' which here wrongly follows in English Version Greek text) to them which heretofore have sinned (namely, before my second visit, <reference osisRef="2Cor.12.21">2Co 12:21</reference>), and to all others (who have sinned since my second visit, or are in danger of sinning)." The English Version, "as if I were present the second time," namely, this next time, is quite inconsistent with <reference osisRef="2Cor.13.1">2Co 13:1</reference>, "this is the third time I am coming to you," as Paul could not have called the same journey at once "the second" and "the third time" of his coming. The antithesis between "the second time" and "now" is palpable.<div eID="gen34817" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34818" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">if I come again, &c.--</hi>that is, whensoever I come again (<reference osisRef="Acts.20.2">Ac 20:2</reference>). "I trust that" your own Christianity will be recognized by you (observe, "ye shall know," answers to "know your own selves," <reference osisRef="2Cor.13.5">2Co 13:5</reference>) as sufficient "proof" that ye are not reprobates, but that "Christ speaks in me," without needing a proof from me more trying to yourselves. If ye doubt my apostleship, ye must doubt your own Christianity, for ye are the fruits of my apostleship. <div eID="gen34833" type="x-p"/>
